title: The Vikings Are Winning Like It’s 1973
contentHtml:
For three weeks, the NFL was in a holding pattern around who would be the last undefeated team left standing. One of those teams was the revived-dynasty Kansas City Chiefs, whom I warned might return to being football main-characters again this season. Another was the San Francisco 49ers, who perennially boast one of the league’s most talented rosters and possibly its best coach (in Kyle Shanahan) — plus a pretty damn good QB in the form of Brock Purdy.

Subscribe now

But in a wild Week 7 of action, both the Niners and the Chiefs fell, leaving just one remaining undefeated team. And that team is — wait, who? The Minnesota Vikings??

Yes, the Vikings are now the sole remaining unbeaten squad in the NFL this season, after coming back from a fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Indianapolis Colts last Sunday. It’s just the seventh time in franchise history that Minnesota has started a season 6-0, and the first time they’ve done it since the promising — if ill-fated — Brett Favre-led 2009 campaign.

Like those ‘09 Vikings, the ‘26 version has a familiar quarterback who made his name elsewhere. But that’s probably where those comparisons end. Rather than being a revival of a Minnesota team with one of the league’s top QBs leading a high-scoring offense,1 this year’s Vikings are harkening back to a different era of Minnesota football. And I mean very different.
